question: How does Cursor interpret a hooks.json `command` string — does it apply shell word-splitting, quoting, variable expansion, and command substitution before spawning the hook?

assertion.projection: (reduce .[] as $p ({}; if $p.case == null then . else .[$p.case] = $p end)) as $c | {controls: (([.[] | select(.argc == 0)] | length) >= 2), argv0: ((($c.split.argv0 // "") | endswith("dump-hook.sh"))), split: ($c.split.argv == ["split", "alpha", "beta"]), dquote: ($c.dquote.argv == ["dquote", "two words"]), squote: ($c.squote.argv == ["squote", "two words"]), var: (($c.var.argv[1] // "") | (. != "$HOME" and startswith("/"))), subst: ($c.subst.argv == ["subst", "SUBSTITUTED"]), meta: ($c.meta.argv == ["meta", "a;b|c&d"]), utf8: ($c.utf8.argv == ["utf8", "café-日本-ñ"]), envprefix: ($c.envprefix.probe_env == "probe-value"), envprefix_control: ($c.split.probe_env == ""), anchor: ($c.anchor.argv == ["anchor", "/tmp/user-script.sh", "my-hook-id", "arg with spaces"])}
